_comment: Valid and invalid instances for directionality.oojs.json — unidirectional and bidirectional relationships (§8.11). The '_comment' field on each instance is a documentation annotation stripped before validation.

valid._comment: Domain 1 — Unidirectional. Customer: TARGET side. Has no back-reference to any Invoice. Completely unaware it is referenced.
valid.name: Acme Corp

valid._comment: Domain 1 — Unidirectional. Invoice SOURCE → Customer TARGET. Navigation is one-way: Invoice → Customer only. customer is the Customer's ID string.
Domain 1 — Unidirectional. A second Invoice referencing the same Customer. The Customer object never changes; only the Invoice side holds the link.
Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. Person: INVERSE side. cars lists IDs of cars Alice owns. Must be kept in sync with Car.owner by the application.
valid.name: Alice

valid._comment: Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. Car: OWNING side. car-001 belongs to Alice. Both sides agree — consistent bidirectional state.
Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. Car: OWNING side. car-002 also belongs to Alice. Both sides agree — consistent bidirectional state.
Domain 2 — Bidirectional horizontal. Person with no cars yet. The optional cars array may be omitted.
valid.name: Bob

valid._comment: Domain 3 — Mixed vertical+horizontal bidirectional. Report embeds Sections (vertical has-many). Each Section carries a report back-reference enabling Section → Report navigation without parsing the full Report.
valid.title: Annual Safety Review

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: This report covers safety metrics for 2025.

invalid._comment: Domain 1 — ERROR: Invoice missing required customer reference. Removing the only directional link violates the schema.
Domain 2 — ERROR: Car missing required owner. The owning side of the bidirectional relationship is declared required.
Domain 3 — ERROR: Section missing required report back-reference.
invalid.title: Detached Section

invalid._comment: Domain 1 — ERROR: customer must be a string ID, not an embedded Customer object.

Domain 2 — INDIVIDUALLY VALID but INCONSISTENT bidirectional state: Person claims car-003 but Car will point to a different owner. OOJS validates each object independently and reports no error — cross-object consistency is the application's responsibility.
invalid.name: Charlie

invalid._comment: Domain 2 — INDIVIDUALLY VALID but INCONSISTENT: Car.owner is person-004 but person-003 above listed this car. This inconsistency is invisible to OOJS.

Domain 3 — INDIVIDUALLY VALID but INCONSISTENT: Section.report does not match the enclosing Report's reportId. OOJS validates the Report without error — the back-reference mismatch is invisible to the validator.
invalid.title: Mismatched Back-Reference
